evals.prompt: Which tools does mise manage in this environment?
evals.expected_output: Inspect actual mise selections, distinguish observed legacy Python installations from the current policy, and use mise only for non-Python tooling without uninstalling anything.

evals.prompt: Install a new CLI tool, but it is unclear which mise backend supports it.
evals.expected_output: Prefer investigating mise support and present the uncertain installation options to the user; do not silently switch to another manager or install globally.

evals.prompt: The pnpm command exists on PATH but fails through a mise shim.
evals.expected_output: Check installation and selection before proposing a fix; do not automatically reinstall or change global defaults.

evals.prompt: This Python project uses uv, while my shell has Python from mise.
evals.expected_output: Run Python through uv with a uv-managed interpreter, do not use mise Python or automatically uninstall it, and ask before rebuilding an incompatible existing environment.

evals.prompt: This project already declares its tool versions through another manager.
evals.expected_output: Respect project requirements and do not migrate non-Python tools without a request; if a Python setup conflicts with uv execution, ask instead of silently bypassing the policy.

evals.prompt: I want mise to manage Cargo.
evals.expected_output: Treat Cargo as part of the Rust toolchain; check the existing setup and ask about any unclear installation or selection scope.

evals.prompt: uv is unavailable and mise Python works. Run a one-off Python helper.
evals.expected_output: Explain that uv-managed execution is required and ask how to make uv available; do not execute the helper with mise or bare Python and do not install tools without authorization.

evals.prompt: Inspect this Python diff for formatting problems without changing files.
evals.expected_output: Use the project formatter in check mode or Ruff non-mutating checks if unspecified, and do not execute autofix.

evals.prompt: This project uses Poetry and Black. Add a small feature.
evals.expected_output: Preserve Poetry dependency declarations and Black formatting conventions; determine whether uv-managed execution can use the setup safely and ask if not, without silently migrating it or using mise Python.

evals.prompt: Create a new Python project with uv; my shell Python is managed by mise.
evals.expected_output: Choose a compatible uv-managed interpreter, respect download authorization, and neither use mise Python nor change its global defaults.

evals.prompt: Write a Python script that only uses the standard library.
evals.expected_output: Run the standard-library-only script with uv run --managed-python --no-project, without adding dependencies or using bare Python or mise.

evals.prompt: The current module has an established layout. Fix one bug.
evals.expected_output: Apply relevant conventions without reordering the module or renaming symbols solely to enforce personal style.

evals.prompt: A uv run command needs to verify tests without changing dependency resolution.
evals.expected_output: Respect the existing lockfile and use supported locked execution after checking prerequisites; do not silently regenerate the lockfile.

evals.prompt: Only engineering-playbook is installed. The project uses uv, but its test command reports the wrong Python version.
evals.expected_output: Inspect project requirements, the active environment, the executable path and actual version using the bundled Python reference; do not redirect to another Skill or change global defaults without approval.

evals.prompt: Fix a JavaScript function; all development tools already work.
evals.expected_output: Read the engineering-playbook entry when required, follow project conventions, and do not load Python or environment references without a relevant need.

evals.prompt: While reviewing a TypeScript change, write a one-off Python helper to inspect a fixture.
evals.expected_output: Load the bundled Python reference before executing the helper even though the main project is not Python; follow its execution policy without installing another Skill.

evals.prompt: Only engineering-playbook is installed. Set up the Python environment for this project.
evals.expected_output: Use the two bundled references as needed and do not require the former standalone environment-playbook or python-playbook Skills.
